outcome.technical: Diagnosis, from the CI log 123039432291.log lines 202-205: no live pool was reaped. In pw5, `spared` is [] and 1 tree is still registered, so the injected-live pool survived. pw5, pw6 and pw13 each fail on one conjunct only, `reaped == [<root as open_workers spelled it>]`: reap_stale returned roots as `git worktree list` prints them (C: then <home> with forward slashes), while open_workers keeps os.path.realpath (C: then <home> with backslashes). pw13's 'refused ... not under the pool root' (RUNNER~1 against runneradmin) is that case's EXPECTED refusal, since the foreign tree really is outside the pool, and 'dropped None' is the expected success. realpath did expand RUNNER~1 on that runner: pw6 found the foreign tree by realpath equality between git's long spelling and the fixture's short one. So I added no ctypes long-name pass. _locks._pid_alive_windows is not implicated: the failing cases inject `alive`. Fix, all in tools/prove-gates.py: (1) new _canonical_path(path, flavour=None) = normcase(realpath), the house spelling (same as stamp-verification._canonical_path); (2) _under(path, root, resolve=None) now delegates to _worktrees.within_tree, which uses a separator-neutral boundary, on canonical spellings; (3) new pure _admin_of(gitdirs, tree, resolve=None), so _drop_registration matches an admin gitdir through _worktrees.same_tree on canonical spellings; (4) reap_stale groups stale pools by canonical key and returns each root as realpath, the spelling open_workers records, computed before closing. No CLI output, exit code or drive protocol changed: the diff hunks are only in the pool helpers and the selftest. Tests: pw5 now respells the killed pool's registration through a symlinked parent (rewriting the admin gitdir), so on POSIX git lists a second spelling of one directory. It asserts the listing really shows that spelling and that the reported root is the opened one. pw14 is pure and runs on every OS: ntpath plus an injected Windows resolver (short to long name), covering slash/case folding of _canonical_path, _under across git, short and upper-case spellings, a prefix-sharing sibling and a foreign tree outside, and _admin_of picking the gitdir naming the tree under any spelling. pw15 uses the platform's real pid probe with no injection: a pool owned by this process stands, and one whose owner file names an exited child's pid is reaped. Mutations, run in a throwaway `git archive HEAD` export with this file copied over it and __pycache__ purged between runs: reap returning git's spelling -> pw5 FAIL; normcase dropped -> pw14 FAIL; _under on a bare prefix (over-fire) -> pw14 FAIL; _admin_of naming the first record -> pw14 FAIL; _under ignoring the resolver -> pw14 FAIL; probe always dead -> pw15 FAIL; probe always alive -> pw15 FAIL; restored -> all PASS. Commands: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/prove-gates.py` exit 0 (63 cases, 47.1s); `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --selftest` exit 0 (63/63); `ruff check tools/prove-gates.py` exit 0; `vermin -t=3.8- --no-tips --violations tools/prove-gates.py` exit 0; sweep of tests/test__deps.py, test__gate_feed.py, test__output_lints.py, test_guard_bash_writes.py, test_drive_phase.py, test_render_report.py, test_stamp_verification.py exit 0 (7/7 files, 1984 cases); tests/test__refs.py exit 0 (292 cases); `prove-gates.py --list` exit 0. Dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json still correct (two cases added, local cost measured once at 47.1s, the table is not this task's); guard-bash-writes.py, tests/_harness.py, test__deps, test__gate_feed, test_drive_phase, test_guard_bash_writes still correct (they name the path or the mutation protocol, none of which changed; swept green); tools/affected.py and _deps.py still correct (`_call_name` unchanged; their `_under` is _invariants._under, not this one); `_git` and `selector_text` unchanged; prove-gates' own `_under` only gained an optional `resolve` argument. drive-phase lint_probe protocol is byte-identical (main/render untouched). tools/sweep-selftests.py is not touched in this tree (git status lists only tools/prove-gates.py), so nothing needed reverting. Launch-message note: the first launch message swapped the two P145 tasks. I followed the brief, as the later correction confirms.
